translation: If so, then when Guizhi (cinnamon twig) goes down the throat, if the exterior is harmonious one dies (the Guizhi Decoction is the one of five ingredients such as Guizhi in the section on Zhongjing's counting of days in this volume). The interweaving of interior vacuity and excess has extremely subtle signs; the opposition of sweating, vomiting, and purging brings disaster extremely quickly. And if the medical art is shallow and narrow, the treatment is then mistaken, causing the patient to perish, and one says it is his own lot. Moreover, whenever the two-contraction disease (lianggan) occurs together, the treatment has first and last; releasing the exterior and attacking the interior are originally different. Yet those who cling to delusion and recklessly follow their own ideas say that Shendan and Gansui, taken together, both release the exterior and also remove the interior. The words are clever and seem right, but in principle they truly violate. How can the change of safety and danger be deceived! Now, disease with fever and aversion to cold arises from yang; disease without heat and with aversion to cold arises from yin. What arises from yang can attack the exterior; what arises from yin should warm the interior.
